Educating boys in Hampshire with SEMH needs.
We nurture potential & build confidence.
Welcome to King’s Academy Lord Wilson!
As Headteacher, it is my great privilege to lead this exceptional school, which serves boys with social, emotional, and mental health needs.
Our academy is committed to providing a nurturing environment where every student has the opportunity to thrive both academically and personally. We focus on building resilience, self-confidence, and essential life skills, equipping our young people to face the future with positivity.
At King’s Academy Lord Wilson, we are proud of our close-knit community where students receive tailored support through our experienced staff and diverse curriculum.
Whether it’s through academic guidance, pastoral care, or extracurricular activities, we strive to ensure every pupil finds success and a sense of belonging.
I look forward to working with you and your child on this exciting journey of learning and development.
Dr Nigel Matthias Headteacher

King's Academy Lord Wilson
Music and Performing Arts
We believe that Performing Arts has the power to enrich lives, stimulate creativity, and promote emotional well-being. Our music program is designed to cater to the diverse needs and interests of all our pupils.
Peripatetic Music Lessons
We understand that some pupils may have a particular passion for music. To nurture these talents, we offer peripatetic music lessons with qualified music teachers. These lessons provide individualised instruction and support, allowing pupils to develop their skills at their own pace.
Arts Award and NCFE Certificate in Performance Skills
For pupils who excel in music and wish to take their studies further, we offer the Arts Award and the NCFE Certificate in Performance Skills. These qualifications provide a structured framework for developing musical skills and knowledge, culminating in public performances and assessments.

King's Academy Lord Wilson
Uniform
Why is Uniform Important at King’s Academy Lord Wilson?We believe a consistent and focused learning environment is vital for all our students. Following the school uniform policy plays a significant role in achieving this. Just like the importance of adhering to the passport control system, wearing the correct uniform creates a sense of belonging and reduces distractions.
To ensure everyone can participate fully in the school day, we have developed a new system to address situations where students arrive without proper uniforms. To address the occasional need for spare uniforms, we’ve implemented a system similar to what you might find at a bowling alley. We have a dedicated stock of clean, freshly laundered spare uniforms in various sizes.
If your child arrives out of uniform, they will be issued the appropriate spare set for the day. These uniforms, along with any spare shoes that may be required, undergo a rigorous cleaning and sanitisation process each week to ensure hygiene concerns are completely addressed. This ensures your child can participate comfortably in the school day without any disruption.
On a rare occasion where we do not have appropriate spare uniform, any students arriving out of uniform will receive a dated and time-limited “uniform pass” at passport control. This triggers a phone call from your child’s tutor, who will discuss the situation and potential solutions with you.
Where to purchase a uniform
Uniform can be purchased directly from the school at reception or email: enquiries@kgalordwilson.uk
Financial Hardship (including second-hand uniform)We understand that unforeseen circumstances can arise. If your family is experiencing financial hardship that impacts your ability to provide the correct uniform, please do not hesitate to speak with your child’s tutor in confidence. We are here to support you and can explore potential solutions.
Tracksuit Bottoms or TrousersFor the bottom half of the uniform, plain black tracksuit bottoms or trousers are perfectly acceptable. This provides a comfortable and practical option for students. However, to maintain a smart and consistent appearance, coloured tracksuit bottoms, jeans, or any other style of trousers are not permitted. Small logos, less than 5 cm in diameter, are acceptable on the bottoms, but large or prominent logos, such as the Adidas “three-stripe” design or similar branding, are not allowed. This ensures a clean and streamlined look for the entire student body.
Thank YouWe appreciate your cooperation in ensuring your child arrives in proper uniform each day. This will create a positive learning environment for all students.For further information or clarification on the uniform policy, please do not hesitate to contact the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast and Lunch – King's Academy Lord Wilson
pageCache.text:
King's Academy Lord Wilson
Breakfast and Lunch
We recognise that a nutritious breakfast can set students up for a great day of learning. Every student is welcome at our Breakfast Club which runs each morning until tutor time. On the menu every day is toast and crumpets. Milk, water and squash is also available. We often offer a hot option of beans on toast, porridge or eggs on toast. Breakfast Club is run much like a restaurant where your order is taken when you are seated at the table and it is then brought to you after being freshly prepared.
During morning break, we run our Brunch Club. Everyone is welcome to attend and students can choose from bagels and toast. Milk, squash and water are also available. Students can be supported to make their own breakfast or brunch snack and to support the development of life skills. In addition, students can also socialise with their peers, speak with key staff and can discuss current events.
Breakfast and Brunch Clubs are supported by the Magic Breakfast charity.There is no charge for attending Breakfast Club or Brunch Club and it is open to everyone.
At lunchtime, our spacious dining hall is a hub of activity! Students can choose each day from a variety of menu options, including two separate hot meal choices. The menu is refreshed each season. Freshly baked baguettes and jacket potatoes are also available every day. Students and staff sit down together to eat – another valuable opportunity to develop social skills.
Students entitled to free school meals are welcomed to order lunch free of charge. Those students who are not eligible for free school meals, can pay daily, or arrange a payment plan with the office.
We also have alternative spaces for students to eat lunch, including Quiet Lunch Club held in our Cookery classroom.

King's Academy Lord Wilson
Safeguarding Our Boys: A Priority at King’s Academy Lord Wilson
At King’s Academy Lord Wilson, the safety and well-being of our students is our paramount concern. We understand that young men aged 11-16 navigating social, emotional, and mental health challenges require a nurturing, reliable and secure environment. This statement outlines our unwavering commitment to safeguarding each student entrusted to our care.
A Culture of Care and Support
We cultivate a culture of openness and trust, where boys feel comfortable expressing their needs and concerns. Our dedicated staff, including teachers, safeguarding leaders and partnerships with qualified social workers and counsellors, are trained to identify potential issues and provide appropriate support. We also strive to create a strong sense of community, where boys feel valued and respected by peers and adults alike.
Robust Safeguarding Procedures
Working in Partnership
We recognise the importance of collaboration to ensure comprehensive support for our students. We maintain strong relationships with external agencies, such as social services, mental health professionals, and the police. This allows us to access specialist support when needed and ensure a coordinated approach to safeguarding.
Confidentiality and Respect
We understand the importance of confidentiality while managing safeguarding concerns. We will only share information with others on a need-to-know basis and with the consent of the student unless there is a safeguarding risk. All discussions are held with the utmost respect and sensitivity.
Empowering Our Students
We empower our students with the knowledge and skills to recognise and report abuse or neglect. We provide age-appropriate personal, social, and health education (PSHE) sessions, fostering open communication and healthy relationships. We also encourage students to seek help from a trusted adult within the school if they have any concerns.
We are committed to continuous improvement in our safeguarding practices. We encourage parents, guardians, and students to raise any questions or concerns they may have. We value your feedback in creating a safe and supportive environment for all our boys.
This statement is a brief overview. For more detailed information on our safeguarding policies, please refer to the school’s Child Protection Policy, or contact King’s Academy Lord Wilson’s Safeguarding Lead, Mr Benn BLee@kgalordwilson.uk

PROVIDER ACCESS STATEMENT
This policy statement sets out the arrangements for managing the access of providers to students at Lord Wilson School, for the purpose of giving information about the provider’s education or training offer; this complies with the school’s legal obligations under Section 42B of the Education Act 1997 and the updated Provider Access Legislation which came into force in January 2023.
All students in Years 7 to 13 are entitled:
For students of compulsory school age, we will offer two encounters during Years 8 and 9 and two encounters during Years 10 and 11. We recognise that all of our students have their own identified SEND and we will strive to adapt sessions and encounters to ensure that all students who wish to access will be able to do so.
These provider encounters will be scheduled during school hours, by 28 February if taking place in Years 9 or 11, and the provider will be given a reasonable amount of time to:
Lord Wilson School uses the Gatsby Benchmarks, a framework of best practice, to plan the Careers programme. As part of our commitment to informing students about the full range of learning and training pathways available, we welcome access requests from Sixth Form and Further Education Colleges, University Training Colleges, Institutes of Technology, apprenticeship providers, independent training providers, universities and employers.
By hearing directly from providers, every student is able to build a broad picture of the options available and consider how the opportunity to study or train in different ways, and in different environments, may suit their skills, interests and aptitudes.
Opportunities for providers to speak with students may include school assemblies, employer and provider engagement events or activities to support GCSE, Post-16 choices. However, we recognise that our students may respond best on a bespoke and 1-1 basis and will work with providers to accommodate this.
We are committed to providing meaningful encounters to all students in-person or online; an encounter is defined as one meeting or session between students and a provider. Previously, a number of providers were available to speak to students about technical education and apprenticeships including BAE, PETA, City of Portsmouth College, Red Penguin Marine, Royal Navy.

We are committed to ensuring our students understand the full range of options available to them and welcome opportunities to learn about technical and vocational pathways. In the first instance, requests by providers should be sent to the school’s Careers Leader, Rebecca Lawley, at rlawley@kgalordwilson.uk with a minimum of 6 weeks’ request time. All requests will be considered on the basis of staff availability to support the activity, any clashes with other planned activity, trips or visits, interruption to the preparation for examinations or rooming and space availability to host the activity. Providers should refer to the schools Safeguarding Policy.
We will make a suitable space and equipment available for interactions between providers and students, appropriate to the activity; this will be discussed and agreed in advance of the visit with the Careers Leader or a member of the Careers Team. Providers are very welcome to leave prospectuses and relevant literature at main Reception marked for the attention of the Careers Team.
Our Careers Provision is monitored for quality and impact by the Senior Leadership and Governance Teams and a review of access and opportunities to engage with technical, vocational and training providers forms part of this process; this policy statement is reviewed annually by the Careers Leader and agreed by the Board of Trustees.
Reviewing our Careers Provision
We regularly complete the Compass for special schools assessments, which uses the Gatsby Benchmarks to help track our progress towards achieving the eight Gatsby Benchmarks. The Gatsby Benchmarks have been designed to support institutions to deliver a high-quality careers provision that supports every young person find their best next step. Compass assessments help us to identify our strengths and celebrate success, as well as identifying areas of future focus in order to improve our provision. In addition to Compass assessment data, we use Year 11 destinations data and parent/carer feedback to inform next steps.
This information is reviewed annually by the Careers Leader and the Senior Leadership Team.

King's Academy Lord Wilson
Passport to Learning
King’s Academy Lord Wilson is a mobile phone-free site. This policy is designed to enhance student focus, strengthen social connections, and reduce cyberbullying and online risks.
We want to see our values visible from the moment our learners step onto our school site. Just like at an airport, our pupils clear security and passport control with their ‘3 Rs Passport’ each morning. Our ‘3 Rs Passport’ benefits our school’s community by ensuring we all feel safe and are ready to learn.
What does this look like as a student at King’s Academy Lord Wilson?
The process for students is:
If you’re not quite ready to complete your 3 R’s Passport there’s no need to worry. We’ll make sure that we have everything you need; spare school uniforms and storage for your items.
Please be assured that we will provide you with all the necessary equipment, to be successful across your school day. At the end of the day you will collect your items from the same location as in the morning, before getting into your taxi.
To make sure that everyone is ready to learn we cannot allow anyone onto the school site without having their 3 Rs Passport stamped. To celebrate getting through passport control, each day we will stamp your passport and your tutor will issue you with a golden ticket. This gives a chance to win an Amazon voucher in each Friday’s assembly. Your passport will also show you when you have earned your ‘Golden breakfast.’
A Mobile Phone Free Site
From the time students arrive on campus until the end of the school day, mobile phones are turned off and stored securely in our safe. During breaks and lunch, we encourage everyone to step away from screens, socialise, relax, and engage in school clubs and activities.
We believe this policy will positively impacts on our school community by promoting a more focused learning environment, stronger social connections, and a safer online space for all students. We appreciate your understanding and cooperation in making our school a place where students can learn, grow, and thrive without the distractions of mobile phones.

Our Keystone provision provides a tailored learning experience for Year 7 and 8 students, and a specialised Year 7/8 class for those with significant learning difficulties. This approach ensures each individual receives the specific support they need to thrive.

Keystone students focus on core skills with daily English and Maths sessions. Practical subjects like art, PE, food technology, and science are integrated for a well-rounded experience. Students needing additional support in phonics or communication receive targeted 1-to-1 intervention with our highly trained SENDCo (Special Educational Needs Coordinator). Teachers work closely with the SENDCo to seamlessly integrate these interventions into their classrooms, ensuring optimal progress.
